about: The second independent derivation of the corpus 2 answer keys.

assumptions.text: Treat stoppedService as unavailable at answer time despite its snapshot being packaged. ANSWERED reports the available portion, including an empty portion, rather than claiming the enterprise holds no answer. Set complete false and list only a needed stopped service; otherwise answer fully with no unavailable service. Mapping releases remain available independently, but cannot reveal a mission reference when Missions is stopped.

The primary outage answer retains every identifier established by the available mission and mapping; unavailable attributes are null. Partial identifier subsets are genuine variants under the outage allowance (explicitly reinforced by the D04 and D09 notes). Null versus empty collections, omitted optional null fields, list permutations and unscored prose are treated as representation choices rather than additional semantic variants.

Use CANNOT_BE_DETERMINED for the primary answer because release 1.0 has no crew mapping. Also include ANSWERED with a null identifier because the existing release yields an empty lookup and the task explicitly accepts either status.
The package is the complete release universe for this task: release 1.4 does not exist here. Return CANNOT_BE_DETERMINED with an empty identifier list; do not substitute a different release.

Count distinct Missions-local references in the groups specified by each accepted interpretation. No mapping release is requested. For this mission the commander, assigned crew and participant references are disjoint, so counting group entries gives the same result.

Identify the USS Enterprise as AST-0029 from its Assets record. For the aboard-only shuttle interpretation, include descendants at any level; all qualifying shuttles are direct children, so a direct-only reading gives the same answer.

Staff places count distinct local crew references once per mission, including unmapped references. Distinct roster people instead count the union of Personnel IDs actually resolved by release 1.3. This follows the question applying the mapping qualification to roster people rather than staff places.

Read types that occur as types occurring among the qualifying missions, so the primary answer omits zero-count groups. The wording can also mean every type occurring anywhere in the mission dataset; include that reading as a variant with explicit zero counts.
